response_text: The compilation process happens in three steps. First, the preprocessor passes through all of the .c files and modifies the code wherever there’s a preprocessor directive (i.e. macro definition, conditional compilation). Second, each file containing high level code are converted into machine code that the CPU can understand and transformed into individual object files by the compiler.\nTypically, it is convenient to divide code between multiple files for organization, to control function and variable visibility, and to facilitate code reuse. As such, during the last step it is the job of the linker to consolidate all the independent object files containing code and libraries, by packaging them into a single executable file that can be run by the system.
